question: Select the most appropriate option for blank (4)
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word "**series**" means a number of things, events, or people of a similar kind that follow one after the other. (श्रृंखला)
 
• The phrase **"the conversation usually begins with a series of questions" **makes logical sense as it implies a succession of questions typically asked to get to know someone.
 
• The other options: "**pairs**," "**classes**," and "**parts**" do not fit the context as appropriately. They do not convey the idea of a sequence or succession of questions.

**Complete Sentence:** Consider what happens when you meet someone for the first time. The conversation usually begins with a **series** of questions such as, "Where did you grow up?" "How long have you lived here?" "Where did you go to school?"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pairs (जोड़े)**: means two things that are together, not suitable in the context of asking questions.
 
• **Classes (प्रकार)**: means categories or groups, not fitting in this context.
 
• **Parts (भाग)**: means pieces or segments of a whole, also not fitting the context of sequential questioning.
